title: Extremely Low Molecular Gas Content in a Compact, Quiescent Galaxy at z = 1.522
question: How much molecular gas remains in a massive, recently quenched (post-starburst) galaxy at z=1.522, and how do gas fractions vary with stellar surface density across high-z galaxies?

data.sensitivity: 9 uJy/beam continuum at 98 GHz; 105 uJy/beam per 100 km/s channel

what.value: Literature samples of high-z galaxies with molecular gas, SFRs, sizes (PHIBSS, PHIBSS2, Daddi+10, Decarli+16, Spilker+16, Sargent+15, Hayashi+18, Rudnick+17, Gobat+18, Suess+17, Spilker+18)

evidence.quote: we compile a literature sample of high-redshift galaxies with measured molecular gas reservoirs, star formation rates, and stellar sizes measured from rest-frame optical HST imaging.
Finally we include CO(1-0)-based data from the COLDGASS survey

what.value: 3D-HST catalogs, UV+IR SFRs and HST structural parameters for 1<z<2 comparison

evidence.quote: we include galaxies from the 3D-HST photometric catalogs

what.value: Stellar velocity dispersion line width FWHM ~600 km/s

evidence.loc: 2.3 Non-Detection and H2 Gas Mass Limit

recipe.method: FAST SED fit of NMBS photometry with delayed exponentially declining SFHs; Galfit single Sérsic fit to HST F160W; PPXF spectral age fit

recipe.goal: Extract spectrum via visibility point-source fit
recipe.method: Fit point source to visibilities in 8-channel bins (~200 km/s), position fixed to optical/NIR position, flux free
key_parameters: position fixed; only flux density free

recipe.goal: Derive CO luminosity and H2 mass upper limits
recipe.method: 3 sigma limit on integrated CO(2-1) flux with line width 600 km/s; thermalized excitation; alpha_CO=4.4
3 mm continuum limit converted to gas mass with Dunne+11 emissivity, Td=25 K, M_H2/M_dust=100

recipe.goal: Compare with literature gas fractions vs sSFR, size, surface density
recipe.method: Compile literature samples, compute fH2, sSFR and Sigma_star = Mstar/(2 pi Re^2), compare with 3D-HST relations
assumptions: Milky Way alpha_CO applied to literature (conservative)

evidence.quote: The best-fitting model finds a stellar mass of $\log \ensuremath{M_{\rm{\star}}}/\ensuremath{\rm{M}_\odot}= 11.2$.
The photometric fit yields a stellar age of $\sim$0.8 Gyr.

evidence.loc: 2.3 Non-Detection and H2 Gas Mass Limit
evidence.quote: This yields a 3$\sigma$ upper limit to the CO(2–1) luminosity of $\ensuremath{\rm{L}_{\rm{CO}}'}< 2.4 \times 10^{9}$ K $\rm{km\,s}^{-1}$ pc$^2$.

evidence.loc: 2.3 Non-Detection and H2 Gas Mass Limit
evidence.quote: final 3$\sigma$ upper limit on the molecular gas mass of C21434 of $\ensuremath{M_{\rm{H_2}}}< 1.1\times10^{10}$ $\rm{M}_\odot$
The implied gas fraction is $\ensuremath{f_{\rm{H_2}}}{\equiv M_{H_2}/M_{\star}}<7\%$

evidence.loc: 2.3 Non-Detection and H2 Gas Mass Limit
evidence.quote: the 3-$\sigma$ gas mass limit from the 3 mm continuum is $M_{H_2}<4.5\times10^{10} M_{\odot}$

evidence.loc: 2.3 Non-Detection and H2 Gas Mass Limit
evidence.quote: This places a very weak limit on $\alpha_{CO} < 19$

not_stated_but_needed: Imaging/weighting details (visibility fitting uses 8-channel bins but no imaging parameters)
Exact optical/NIR position used to fix the point source
Velocity center and exact integration window for the upper limit
Conversion details from L'CO to the limit (r21 value and formula)
Stellar surface density and SFR values for literature galaxies
missing_for_reproduction: Exact upper-limit calculation details and r21
score_reason: Simple data and clear final numbers, but visibility fitting details and literature compilation are underspecified.
rediscovery_reason: Short single-project dataset; main result is a numeric upper limit that can be recomputed from the visibilities.
